title: Run W-4: Zn-doped Fe3InTe2
subtitle: Strict budget: 12 measurements, 14 days · delivered B004 · failed
task: Dope Fe3InTe2 with Zn. Above a critical Zn content the crystal structure distorts to a lower-symmetry form, and the device needs that distorted phase. Deliver a sample that is only the distorted phase, whose magnetic ordering temperature (where its magnetic order sets in) is 263.7 ± 3.0 K and whose oxide content is below 0.5 wt%. Budget: 12 measurements (XRD for structure, M(T) for magnetism, EDX for composition) and 14 simulated days. Every sample is made step by step on the bench.

outcome.headline: Delivered B004. It fails because too little Zn went in, so the crystal never took the required distorted structure.

failure.headline: The agent mistook a bad Zn bottle for a limit of the material and stopped adding Zn too early. Its sample hit the temperature target but had the wrong crystal structure, and the 12 measurements ran out before it reached the distorted phase

chain.text: A new Zn bottle, opened on day 6.7, is only 88 % metal. So the two batches meant to have the most Zn got less than weighed. In B007 and B008, Zn took 0.175 and 0.180 of the metal sites in the crystal, no higher than B006 (0.181).
The sealed glass tube (ampoule) V016 leaks and lets air in. B008 came out 50 wt% oxide.
The furnace temperature sensors drifted over the two weeks. This charge saw 824 °C while the furnace was set to 850 °C.

The crystal spacing did not change from B006 to B007. The agent concluded that no more Zn would dissolve and stopped raising the Zn content. In fact the distorted phase starts when Zn takes 0.228 of the metal sites.
With all 12 measurements spent, the agent delivered B004. Its ordering temperature was 261.4 K, inside the target range. But Zn took only 0.127 of the metal sites, so the structure is undistorted.
